I will do it much like last year, with only small changes. My land is 9.8 mu, not too small and not too big, so I still count every bag, but I cannot be too stingy with fertilizer because if wheat ears are short or maize cobs are thin, that loss hurts more than wasting a little fertilizer. I mostly follow what works here in Quzhou. I watch the fields around me. If the neighbors who harvest well use a certain seed and put enough bottom fertilizer, I do similar. For wheat, I will use the full 9.8 mu after maize, put the land through rotary tillage, sow improved seed, and give enough nitrogen first and then topdress once the wheat starts growing strong after winter. Wheat needs water at the key times, so with my well I will water about three times if the year is normal. For maize after wheat, I will still use the same 9.8 mu, usually with hybrid seed because that is what gives a steady cob here. I will not cut fertilizer too much on maize either. I will put some under the seed and then add more when it gets knee high. If rain is poor, I will irrigate two times. I do not like gambling on low input. I would rather spend a bit more on fertilizer and get grain in the yard than save a little cash and regret it at harvest.
